fact: The education ministry's secretary general said on 2 February 2026 that the rate of integration into e-Msomo stood at 45% in public primary schools, against 100% of public secondary schools nationwide; it is a rate of integration, given with no numerator or denominator, and not a share stated to be entering data.

Al-Watwan reports the ministry's figures of 100% of public secondary schools and 45% of public primary schools integrated into e-Msomo at 2 February 2026; among private schools, all in Ngazidja, with 5 of 35 in Mwali not yet connected and about 24% in Ndzuani still to integrate.

The secretary general thanked schools' administrative teams for creating and entering pupil lists, teacher lists and marks statements into e-Msomo, from which report cards are issued, and noted difficulties with entering marks in some private schools, as of 2 February 2026.
The Ministry of National Education presented the platform's results at its own press conference on 2 February 2026 and set schools a further week to complete the required operations.

On 2 February 2026 the ministry reported integration rates of 100% for public secondary and 45% for public primary schools, gave late schools one more week, and announced that the single report card from the platform will be the only document accepted for enrolment at the University of the Comoros and other higher-education institutions.

Ministry officials told Al-Watwan that on e-Msomo school heads enrol pupils and generate report cards, teachers log in to enter marks that cannot be changed afterwards, and each pupil gets a school identification number with their school career tracked; stated on 25 November 2025.

The Ministry of Education supervises e-Msomo, validates the data and authorises the official printing of report cards, which must carry its seal, according to its deputy secretary general on 25 November 2025.

A ministry director said on 25 November 2025 that the single report card belongs to a wider modernisation of the education system inspired by the Assises nationales and integrated into the Plan Comores Émergent; the article does not say the plan names e-Msomo.

At 25 November 2025 the ministry gave e-Msomo registration as 100% in Ngazidja, 100% in Mwali, 65% in Ndzuwani and only 35% of private schools nationally; these are schools registered, not split by level, and no figure for primary schools or for schools entering data is given.

By 25 November 2025 schools were being registered on e-Msomo island by island (100% Ngazidja and Mwali, 65% Ndzuwani) and the ministry called on late schools to finish, expecting the process to be completed shortly.

We Are Tech Africa states that the Ministry of National Education leads the E-Msomo and E-Shiyo effort, with technical help from the digital agency ANADEN; the article dates the launch no more closely, so its publication date is used.
We Are Tech Africa states that the two platforms are funded by UNICEF; no domestic funding is mentioned, and the date is the article's publication date.
We Are Tech Africa states that the launch of E-Msomo and E-Shiyo is part of the Comoros Digital 2028 plan; it does not say the plan names E-Msomo, and the date is the article's publication date.

Comoros launched E-Msomo, a central system for report cards that assigns each student a unique ID and tracks academic results, reported on 20 June 2025; equipping schools, training teachers and widening internet access (35.7% of Comorians online) are named as next steps.

On 5 June 2025 the education authorities and ANADEN officially launched e-Msomo, which allows marks to be entered online and report cards generated automatically and plans a unique identifier per pupil and the handling of transfers; an extension phase with UNICEF Comoros was under study, according to La Gazette des Comores.
La Gazette des Comores reports that the education authorities launched e-Msomo on 5 June 2025 in collaboration with the digital agency ANADEN, with the Minister of National Education speaking for it.
ANADEN's director called the 5 June 2025 launch of e-Msomo and e-Shiyo a significant step in carrying out the Comores Numérique 2028 strategy; the article does not say the strategy names e-Msomo.

ANADEN's own log of achievements describes e-Msomo, presented on 5 June 2025 at La Coulée primary school, as digital management of school report cards and pupil tracking in its pilot phase; it gives no number of schools.
ANADEN states that the e-Msomo and e-Shiyo platforms launched on 5 June 2025 fall within the Comores Numérique 2028 strategy; it does not say the strategy names e-Msomo.
ANADEN, in partnership with the Ministry of National Education and UNICEF Comoros, officially launched e-Msomo on 5 June 2025 at La Coulée primary school, in a pilot phase.
